paragraphs.text: Lovers set against the qualified, and the lovers win every round. Stain-washing books there are, and their far-siders too; yogins, pundits stand hale — but Thy lovers alone, in truth. Sated with MAyA-time-limit-passion-and-the-rest for food, they stroll glad, Lord, love-ful, on the world’s shore. Weeping or laughing, Thee aloud they babble; these lovers: praise-word-lift-offerings apart indeed are they. No passionless one, no master either, no freedom-hungerer is Thy worshipper. May I be: but brimming-love-wine-sap-mad. Who, dragging the outside into heart’s inside itself, worships Thee, Ruler: with love-nectar-sap-floods him I bow. Between right and unright selves, between doings, between knowings: so between joy-and-pain selves, lovers taste some. Ah! Stir-and-still’s Lord, Master: though blind, though leprous, they shine past measure, wild-Thy-love-jeweled. Gleaners, grain-pickers, foes’ shadow-limbed even, Ruler: by Thy-love’s great heat the king of kings even they lord. In nectar-wet Thy-love though wallowing, yet climb-hungering: with mind alone, All, some worship Thee, standing round about.

Kept and questioned next. To be guarded, to be grown, to be honored: this, Ruler, passing’s ill-faring-smasher, Thy love’s great hoard. Lord, though Thy lover-folk love Thee: yet envy dropped toward Her, gladdened ever be the Mistress. Thy state first, to be: when Thy love’s birth-time comes, won the milk-great jar; slain, in curds, greed. What, is this not attainment past compare? What chief joy streams it not? Love, ever-waxing: this, the Kind One’s, ever-new. In Thy stained mind sunk, Thy-love’s gem-creeper: hard! spreads not even its own, those unmanned own-hoard-blossomings. Love in the Lord, in three-worlds’ Master: is it not highest attainment? Yet for want of wonder-powers, is it not full? This, my worry.

Then pervasion and road. Without, within too: keen-blooming Three-eyed’s-bouquet-scents, fair, scent even cross-scented yogins, near-dwelling, all. Light is there, by no tale, none; the world even, all past-sleep. Where, Lord, at Shiva-night’s post, ever lover-folk worship Thee. Goodness, in true mood, in kindly Lord, widen in worship. On the crown sport Kind-Maker’s-foot-dust-risen-heaps. To sever passion-and-the-rest mind-scents even, gloom gape, Kind One, be mine: or in Thy-self-loss, the three-strand-throng. Passing’s road far-far; limb-stalk burnt with keen-and-sundry ills; joys nowise tasted; what joy was, never long was ours. Thus vain am I grown: moon-bearer’s-foot-pressed-fair-crowned, and Thy lover. So make me now: high-fortuned, long-long.
